When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”
Pilate said to the chief priests and the multitudes, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”
and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one that perverts the people, and behold, having examined him before…

For if I have done wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those…
Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”

people.name: Augustus
people.line: Roman emperor during the birth of Jesus

translations.web: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him,
translations.bsb: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
translations.kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
translations.asv: But I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death: and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him.
